Make line 2 of a Short a dated fact with a number, not a staged scene. The two best Shorts did this ('2008. Lehman dooba…', 'September mein 7.05 billion dollar…') and held 88-89 at the 25% mark. The shagun Short spent line 2 on a wedding-stage scene and was do

Open long videos on the exact rupee result, not a 'what if'. Both home-loan videos opened on '50 lakh ka ghar, bill 1 crore' and kept 51-52 at the 5% mark. The job-loss video opened on 'Kal naukri chali jaaye…' and kept only 35.

In long videos, give the main answer (e.g. how much the bank earns in total) within the first 90 seconds. The average viewer of our 11-12 minute videos leaves after 73-97 seconds, and only 20-30 are still watching at the 10% mark (about 70 seconds in).

Tag every Short as opening on the story's picture or on the presenter. No video was tagged this week, so the test has no result yet. Judge Instagram openings separately from YouTube: the SIP Short was our best on YouTube, yet 82% swiped it away on Instagram.

Use no more than 3-6 words in one or two lines of thick yellow or white text, big enough to read on a phone, with key words in a red or yellow box.

sglearning.report:
Shorts are working: the best three were watched 62-78% of the way through, but long videos only 11-15%.
Long videos lose half their viewers in the first ~35 seconds; the average viewer stays about 1.5 minutes of an 11-12 minute video.
Best: the Sensex/SIP Short (138 views, 77% watched, half stayed to the end). Weakest: the job-loss long video (140 views, 11% watched).
Instagram: the Sahara reel was the only one most people didn't swipe away (36% left early vs 55-84% for the rest). The picture-vs-presenter test has no answer yet because no Short was tagged.
Too new or too few views to judge: the last five uploads, plus the UPI and license Shorts.
The one change this week: make the first sentence of every video, long ones included, a real name or exact rupee figure plus the surprise, like 'Sensex halved, yet SIP investors won?'
